item_name: DiMP / PrDiMP (Bhat et al. ICCV 2019; Danelljan et al. CVPR 2020) - training features through the target model predictor
bibliography: (1) Goutam Bhat, Martin Danelljan, Luc Van Gool, Radu Timofte. Learning Discriminative Model Prediction for Tracking. ICCV 2019, pp. 6182-6191. arXiv:1904.07220 (https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.07220); CVF open access version is the same study. (2) Martin Danelljan, Luc Van Gool, Radu Timofte. Probabilistic Regression for Visual Tracking. CVPR 2020. arXiv:2003.12565 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.12565). Code for both: PyTracking framework, https://github.com/visionml/pytracking (GPL-3.0); DiMP network ltr/models/tracking/dimpnet.py, target classifier modules ltr/models/target_classifier/{initializer.py, optimizer.py, residual_modules.py, linear_filter.py, features.py}; DiMP optimizer class DiMPSteepestDescentGN and PrDiMP optimizer class PrDiMPSteepestDescentNewton in optimizer.py; online tracker pytracking/tracker/dimp/dimp.py with parameters pytracking/parameter/dimp/dimp50.py. Related derivative (not examined as a separate study): SuperDiMP (DiMP classifier + PrDiMP box head, released only in PyTracking, no separate paper). arXiv preprints and conference papers are the same studies (no duplicates counted twice).
full_text_checked: DiMP: full arXiv PDF text extracted and read for Sections 3.1-3.7 (loss, steepest descent, initializer, learned loss, offline training, online tracking), Section 4.1 with Tables 1-3, Section 4.2 benchmark text; Tables 5-7 numeric cells were partly lost in text extraction. Supplementary (S1-S6) not read. PrDiMP: full arXiv PDF text read for Sections 4-5.2 including Table 1 and Figure 5 description and LaSOT/UAV success plot legends; appendix B (Newton optimizer details) not read. Code: PyTracking repository file listing checked; optimizer.py class names and dimp.py localize_advanced flags and dimp50.py thresholds read via raw GitHub. Training scripts not executed.
task_and_output: Generic single-object tracking (SOT) from a first-frame bounding box. Output per frame: a dense target-confidence score map over a search region (5x target size), from which the target center is taken as the arg-max, plus a bounding box refined by a separate IoU-prediction branch (ATOM IoU-Net in DiMP; probabilistic KL-trained box branch in PrDiMP). PrDiMP additionally interprets the center score map as a probability density p(y|x) = exp(s(y)) / Z over center positions. The online tracker also emits a discrete localisation flag per frame: normal / uncertain / hard_negative / not_found (pytracking dimp.py).
data_and_independent_videos: Training: training splits of TrackingNet, LaSOT, GOT10k and COCO (DiMP: 50 epochs x 20,000 sampled videos per epoch; PrDiMP: same settings, 50 epochs x 1000 iterations). Test sets are separate videos: VOT2018 (60 videos), LaSOT test (280 videos, ~2500 frames average), TrackingNet test (511 videos, evaluation server), GOT10k test (180 videos, object classes disjoint from its train split; retrained on GOT10k train only for that benchmark), NFS-30 (100), OTB-100 (100), UAV123 (123). Ablations in DiMP Section 4.1 and PrDiMP Section 5.1 use a pooled set of OTB-100 + NFS + UAV123 = 323 videos, not used for training, averaged over 5 runs. No separate validation split for ablation choices is reported; the same 323 videos serve both analysis and final comparison.
target_size_and_input_resolution: Search patch = 5 x target size (base scale), resized to a fixed patch (288x288 for DiMP in PyTracking settings [uncertain]); classification features from ResNet block 3 (stride 16) plus an extra conv block, giving roughly an 18x18 score map; target model filter kernel 4x4 with 512 channels [uncertain for channel count]. Target thus spans about 3-4 feature cells in each direction at stride 16. Label Gaussian sigma = 1/4 of target size. Input is RGB at full camera resolution before cropping.
frame_rate_and_camera_motion: Benchmarks at native frame rates (mostly 25-30 fps; NFS used in its 30 fps version). Camera motion and background motion present (UAV123 drone videos, TrackingNet YouTube clips); not separately controlled or ablated. Training samples frames within a segment of Tss = 60 frames, train frames from the first half and test frames from the second half.
detector_and_exemplar: No object detector. The target is specified by the ground-truth box in the first frame; the initial training set is 15 augmented samples of the first frame. Afterwards, frames tracked with sufficient confidence are added as pseudo-labelled samples (memory up to 50, oldest discarded); hard-negative frames are added with a higher learning rate (0.02 vs 0.01 in dimp50.py).
trainable_nodes_and_loss: Trained offline end-to-end: ResNet-18/50 backbone (ImageNet init, fine-tuned), classification feature block (Cls), model initializer (conv + PrRoI pooling, averaged over train samples), steepest-descent optimizer hyper-parameters (step computed in closed form; regularisation lambda learned), the free parameters of the discriminative online loss: label y_c, target mask m_c and spatial weight v_c each parameterised by N = 100 triangular radial basis functions of distance from the target center (knot spacing 0.1 feature cells), and the IoU-Net box branch. Online (inner) loss: L(f) = sum ||v_c (m_c s + (1 - m_c) max(0,s) - y_c)||^2 + ||lambda f||^2 with s = x * f. Offline (outer) classification loss: mean squared hinge-type error on the TEST frames, l(s,z) = s - z if z > T, max(0,s) if z <= T (T = 0.05), averaged over all optimizer iterates f(0)...f(Niter) with Niter = 5; total loss beta*Lcls + Lbb with beta = 100. PrDiMP: inner and outer center losses replaced by KL divergence between predicted density exp(s)/Z and a Gaussian label density (sigma = 1/4 target size), optimised with a Newton-type steepest descent; box branch trained with KL using Monte Carlo proposals (sigma_bb = 0.05). Parameter counts not reported in the papers.
controls_seeds_splits: DiMP Table 1: model predictor variants trained identically: initializer only (Init, target appearance only, Siamese-like), gradient descent with learned step (GD), steepest descent (SD). DiMP Table 2: incremental additions from a fixed ImageNet ResNet-18 + SD baseline: +Init, +FT (training the whole network including backbone through the predictor), +Cls, +Loss (learned y/m/v). DiMP Table 3: online update strategies (no update, model averaging, proposed training-set memory). PrDiMP Table 1: four regression losses (L2, robust L2, NLL, KL with label uncertainty) applied to both branches, only the box branch, or only the center branch; Figure 5: sweep of label noise sigma. All on the pooled 323-video set, 5 runs averaged (tracker stochasticity), single training seed per variant, no confidence intervals or significance tests reported. No random/shuffled feature control.
metrics_and_numbers: DiMP (arXiv:1904.07220): Table 1 (OTB+NFS+UAV, AUC %): Init 58.2, GD 61.6, SD 63.8. Table 2 (AUC %): SD with fixed ImageNet ResNet-18 58.7; +Init 60.0 (+1.3); +FT backbone trained through the predictor 62.6 (+2.6, the largest single gain); +Cls 63.3 (+0.7); +Loss learned 63.8 (+0.5). Table 3: no update 61.7, model averaging 61.7, proposed memory update 63.8. Table 4 VOT2018: DiMP-50 EAO 0.440, robustness 0.153, accuracy 0.597; DiMP-18 EAO 0.402; SiamRPN++ 0.414. LaSOT (Fig. 4 legend): DiMP-50 AUC 56.9, DiMP-18 53.2, ATOM 51.5. TrackingNet (Sec. 4.2 text): DiMP-50 AUC 74.0 vs SiamRPN++ 73.3. GOT10k Table 6 (Sec. 4.2 text): ATOM AO 55.6; DiMP-18 relative gain 4.1% over ATOM; DiMP-50 AO 61.1 [uncertain - table cells lost in extraction, value from memory]. Speed: 57 fps (ResNet-18), 43 fps (ResNet-50) on GTX 1080. PrDiMP (arXiv:2003.12565) Table 1 (OTB+NFS+UAV, AUC/OP0.5/OP0.75): both branches - L2 63.1, robust L2 (= DiMP) 63.8, NLL 63.0, KL (ours) 65.5; box branch only (center robust L2) - L2 63.8, NLL 65.0, KL 65.8; center branch only (box KL) - L2 64.8, robust L2 65.8, NLL 63.2, KL 65.5. LaSOT AUC (Fig. 6a legend): PrDiMP-50 59.8, DiMP-50 56.9, PrDiMP-18 56.4; UAV123 (Fig. 6b): PrDiMP-50 68.0 vs DiMP-50 65.3; TrackingNet AUC 75.8 (abstract). Speed ~40 / 30 fps (ResNet-18/50).
tested_conditions: Unseen videos: yes (all benchmarks are test splits; GOT10k with unseen classes). Target absence: not reported as a measured condition (the tracker has a not_found flag, but no evaluation of absence detection; LaSOT/UAV contain out-of-view frames but no absence metric). Similar distractors: no dedicated evaluation; distractor handling is part of the online tracker (second-peak test, hard-negative update) but not ablated in the papers. Occlusion: not reported separately (only inside aggregated benchmarks). Night or low light: not reported. Sequential operation on own predictions: yes - online memory uses the tracker's own pseudo-labels (DiMP Table 3 update strategies), but offline training uses ground-truth boxes for train frames only.
mechanism_summary: Published mechanism: (a) a small target model (one 4x4 conv filter) is not learned by a fixed solver but produced by a differentiable predictor: an initializer from the target region of the training frames followed by a few steepest-descent iterations with closed-form step length, minimising a discriminative loss that uses all background positions in the training frames as negatives; (b) the predictor is unrolled inside training and the whole network (backbone, classification features, initializer, loss parameters) is trained so that the PREDICTED model generalises to LATER test frames of the same video (train frames from the first half, test frames from the second half of a 60-frame segment); (c) the inner loss itself is learned: label shape, target/background mask and spatial weight as radial functions of distance to center; the learned weight increases at the center and decreases in the ambiguous transition ring (Fig. 3); (d) online, the training set is extended with confidently tracked frames and the model refined by a few iterations (every 20 frames, or immediately when a distractor peak is detected). PrDiMP replaces the score-regression loss by a KL divergence between the predicted center density and a label density that models annotation uncertainty. Proposed modification for us (not published): apply (b) and (c) to the FlyVis readout/core with an episode split exemplar -> later search frames, see candidate_node_change.
transfer_limits: (1) Scale of training: DiMP trains a ResNet (11-25 M parameters) on ~1 M sampled episodes from four large datasets; our core has 734 trainable parameters and ~130 train videos (train104 + train26 already re-used), and z13_core_continue_v1 showed that more core training overfits train104 (D_train - D_frozen -1.67 pp [-4.11; +0.83]). The +2.6 AUC gain of +FT (Table 2) is a single-run, no-CI number from a much richer backbone and cannot be transferred as an expected effect size. (2) Features: the gain of end-to-end training concerns RGB appearance features with 512 channels; FlyVis gives 34 cell-type motion/brightness channels on 721 grey hexals, crop about 2x target, target about 9x12 lattice steps - the score map is therefore tiny and nearly every negative location is close to the target ring that DiMP down-weights. (3) Search region: DiMP uses 5x target size so that distractors and background are inside training frames; our crop of about 2x target contains few independent negatives; neighbours are often partially inside the target ring. (4) Time: DiMP updates every 20 frames and on distractor events over sequences of thousands of frames; our loss episodes last up to 30 frames at 30 Hz with 4 exemplar observations, so online refinement has little room. (5) Environment: YOLO/ByteTrack/MASA decide association; DiMP's output is a box, not an association cost, so benefit must be shown through the existing Kalman-center correction entry point (z13_first_divergence_v1: a 79.7 px correction raised the correct match cost 0.123 -> 1.0 at threshold 0.8). (6) Refusal: DiMP has no learned refusal; its not_found / uncertain flags are fixed thresholds (0.25, second-peak ratio 0.8) on a calibrated score.
research_questions_addressed: 5.3 (core training through the applied readout): direct evidence that training features through the target-model predictor beats fixed pretrained features (Table 2, +FT +2.6 AUC) and that a learned inner loss adds a little (+0.5); design analogy for the episode split (fit on train frames, loss on later frames). 5.2 (target model and memory): direct evidence that discriminative fitting with background negatives beats target-only prediction (Table 1: Init 58.2 vs SD 63.8) and that a curated training-set memory beats model averaging (Table 3); caution that both rely on rich RGB features. 5.1 (right object and refusal): only design analogy - calibrated least-squares in the target region is kept deliberately for target-loss detection; the distractor/not-found decision is a separate hand-set rule. PrDiMP adds a caution for 5.1/5.3: a probabilistic KL center loss alone does not beat robust L2 for the center branch (65.5 vs 65.8). 5.4: not addressed (SOT only).
candidate_node_change: Node: readout of FlyVis (target-model fitting) with optional core gradient - 'episode-split meta-trained readout with learned radial loss'. Change: keep the differentiable ridge readout and the DiMP outer loss on later search frames already built (z13_next_differentiable_v1, z13_aligned_core_v1) but (i) fit the target model on all 4 pre-loss exemplar observations instead of the last one only (DiMP multi-sample Strain), and (ii) learn the inner loss shape - label y(d), mask m(d) and weight v(d) as ~10 radial basis coefficients each (DiMP Sec. 3.4) - instead of the hand-set balanced (z13_balanced_ridge_v1) and hinge (z13_hinge_target_v1) variants; core weights frozen in step 1. Step 2 only if step 1 passes: allow core gradient with the same outer loss and a strong anchor to stock C weights. Controls: (a) no-fly: same learned-loss readout on R1 (34 temporal input-eye channels) and on a spatio-temporal input filter bank of equal dimension; (b) stock FlyVis: same learned loss on frozen stock C; (c) current accepted readout (centered uniform ridge on D). Minimal check: train26 useful-center share, paired bootstrap by video, learned-loss D vs centered uniform D and vs C; learned loss coefficients fitted on train104 only, no dev35 tuning; CPU minutes for step 1. Stop condition: if the upper CI bound of learned-loss D minus centered uniform D is below +2 pp, or if learned-loss C gains as much as D (then it is a readout/optimizer effect, not a FlyVis representation effect), stop and do not run step 2 core training. Note: the selection problem (2 useful of 84 at 1 % coverage) is not addressed by this change; success here is localisation only and must not be reported as a refusal or HOTA gain.
strongest_objection: Our project already ran the closest transferable version: core D trained through a differentiable centered ridge target model (z13_aligned_core_v1, D_adapted - D_center -2.33 pp [-4.69; +0.03]) and continued core training (z13_core_continue_v1, negative). DiMP's evidence for end-to-end feature training comes from millions of RGB parameters and a single-run ablation without intervals; with 734 parameters and ~130 videos the expected gain is small and the overfitting risk is demonstrated in our own data. The learned-loss component that remains untried contributed only +0.5 AUC in DiMP Table 2, and PrDiMP Table 1 shows that changing the center loss alone does not help. The bottleneck measured in our project is selection/refusal, which DiMP does not learn.
evidence_strength: Peer-reviewed (ICCV 2019, CVPR 2020), widely reproduced and extended (SuperDiMP, KeepTrack, ToMP, TrDiMP all build on the same code), public code verified to exist (PyTracking, class names checked). Benchmark results: strong. Ablations relevant to us (Table 2 +FT, +Loss; PrDiMP Table 1 center-only): moderate-to-weak - single training run per variant, 5 inference runs, no CI, ablation set doubles as reporting set. Overall: strong for 'discriminative predictor beats target-only template' with RGB features; weak for transfer to 734-parameter motion features.
where_distinction_is_made: Target vs background/distractor: in the target model (discriminative loss over all training-frame positions, distractors inside the 5x search area are negatives) and in the learned loss shape (ring around target down-weighted). Target found vs similar distractor vs absent: a SEPARATE hand-set decision in the online tracker (pytracking dimp.py localize_advanced): max score < 0.25 -> not_found; a second peak above 0.8 x the first -> resolve by distance to previous position, otherwise uncertain; second peak above 0.5 x first -> hard_negative (update with higher learning rate); updates suppressed on not_found/uncertain. Insufficient data: not modelled. A map maximum is distinguished from presence of the right object only by the calibrated absolute score (the paper keeps least-squares in the target region because 'calibrated target confidences' help detect target loss) and by the second-peak ratio; no learned presence head. PrDiMP turns the map into a density, giving an uncertainty shape (variance, multiple modes, Fig. 4) but uses it only qualitatively, with re-scaled not-found threshold.
feature_dependence: Depends on rich RGB appearance features from an ImageNet-pretrained ResNet fine-tuned end-to-end (512-channel classification features). No evidence in either paper for small temporal motion/brightness features. Our own data give partial evidence in the other direction: a DiMP-like ridge target model on FlyVis C/D features beats equal-dimension input-eye features (D - R1 +8.83 pp [+5.43; +13.21], z13_target_model_r1_v1), but the online target model was not better than the prior readout (z13_target_model_probe_v1, -2.19 pp).
association_consequence: None in the papers: SOT output (center + box), no detection matching or identity preservation. In our stand the answer would enter as a correction of the Kalman-predicted center before ByteTrack/MASA matching; z13_center_hota_v1 shows HOTA 61.6584 vs 61.6548 for the stand with the centered D readout (practically zero). An external guard rule - limit correction shift, or reject correction if it raises the match cost above the threshold - can remove harmful corrections like the R1 case without any target model; a DiMP-style change must therefore beat the stand + guard rule, not only the stand.
difference_from_tried: Already tried and matching DiMP ideas: online discriminative ridge target model with neighbours as negatives (z13_target_model_probe_v1, z13_target_model_r1_v1), centered Gaussian label (z13_target_center_v1, dev35 transfer positive), balanced target/background weights (z13_balanced_ridge_v1, not accepted), one-sided hinge background loss (z13_hinge_target_v1, completed_negative - equivalent to DiMP's fixed max(0,s) background term), differentiable readout (z13_next_differentiable_v1), core training through the target model (z13_aligned_core_v1, inconclusive/negative) and continued core training (z13_core_continue_v1, negative). NOT tried: (1) learning the inner loss shape (label, mask, spatial weight as radial functions) from the generalisation error; (2) a multi-frame training set: code check of scripts/z13_aligned_core.py and tracking/z13_aligned_loss.py shows that z13_aligned_core_v1 ALREADY used the DiMP outer-loss design - ridge fitted on the last exemplar frame only (N_EXEMPLAR-1), loss on a later search frame with the DiMP robust squared loss (threshold 0.05, relu on background) and all-zero query label when the target is absent - so the episode split itself is not new; what differs is fitting on all 4 exemplar observations (DiMP Strain with several frames) and averaging the outer loss over solver iterates (irrelevant for a closed-form ridge); (3) initializer + few-step steepest descent instead of an exact ridge solve (likely irrelevant at our size); (4) DiMP-style online memory of confidently tracked samples with hard-negative re-weighting during the loss episode; (5) PrDiMP KL density loss - but PrDiMP's own center-only ablation shows no gain over robust L2, so it is a low-priority difference. Since the episode split and DiMP outer loss were already used in z13_aligned_core_v1, the remaining genuine differences are the learned loss shape and the multi-frame exemplar training set; core training through the target model itself is NOT a new experiment and DiMP is only an explanation source for it (mandatory question of the outline).
memory_write_policy: Online training set (memory) of up to 50 samples: first frame (15 augmented samples) kept; a new sample is written when the frame flag is not 'not_found' and not 'uncertain' (max score >= 0.25 and no ambiguous second peak); hard-negative frames are written with learning rate 0.02 instead of 0.01; oldest samples discarded. Model refined by 2 optimizer iterations every 20 frames or 1 iteration immediately on a hard-negative frame (dimp50.py, paper Sec. 3.7). No separate distractor memory.
distractor_representation: Implicit only: distractors are negatives in the discriminative loss (background region of training frames) and trigger a hard-negative update; no explicit distractor buffer, track or class.
refusal_evidence_horizon: Single frame: thresholds on the current score map maximum and second-peak ratio; no accumulation over frames and no sequential test.
loss_on_applied_decision: No. Offline loss is on the intermediate score map of test frames (squared hinge-type regression, PrDiMP: KL of the center density) plus box IoU regression; the applied decisions (arg-max center, not_found flag, memory write) are not in the loss. It is however defined on future frames relative to the fitted model, i.e. closer to the applied use than a same-frame loss.
association_entry_point: Not applicable in the source (SOT). For us: box/center correction of the track's Kalman prediction before matching (state update / correction entry point), identical to the current z13 entry point.
no_fly_control_equivalent: (1) The same learned-loss target model on input-eye features R1 and on a spatio-temporal filter bank of equal dimension without the connectome; (2) a Kalman-only stand with a shift-limit or match-cost guard rule on corrections; (3) the same readout on stock FlyVis C to separate representation change from readout/optimizer change. Required by rule 6.16: stand / change without fly / change with fly.
hard_subset_evaluation: No separate hard subset in either paper; ablations use the pooled OTB-100 + NFS + UAV123 set (323 videos, chosen for diversity, not difficulty). LaSOT attribute analysis not reported in these papers.
temporal_information_availability: Causal: the target model is predicted from past frames only (first frame + past confident frames) and applied to the current frame; latency is one forward pass (57/43 fps DiMP, 40/30 fps PrDiMP). Offline training uses future frames only as supervision targets, not as inputs at test time, so the benefit is available to a tracker that must act now.
depth_level: Full analysis (code, ablations, all fields), as set in the item.
